extracted.intended_audience: authors submitting papers to the AAAI-10 conference (AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing AAAI-10 conference submissions to preserve author anonymity during blind peer review. Covers what to include/exclude on the first page, reference rules, and how to cite one's own prior work.

rubrics_metrics.name: First page content
rubrics_metrics.description: The first page, on which the paper body begins, should include the title, abstract, content areas, and ID number (if available), but not the acknowledgments and names or affiliations of the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include title, abstract, content areas, and paper ID (if available) on the first page. Do not include acknowledgments, author names, or affiliations on this page. Identifying material may be added later for the camera-ready version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author anonymity / conceal identities
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewing for the AAAI Conference is blind to the identities of the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Try to avoid including any information in the body of the paper or references that would identify the authors or their institutions. This includes explicit names, institutional addresses, or other signals that would reveal authorship. Such information may be added to the final camera-ready version for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: References: include published works only
rubrics_metrics.description: The references should include all published literature relevant to the paper, including previous works of the authors, but should not include unpublished works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite all relevant published literature (including the authors' previous published work). Do not cite unpublished manuscripts or technical reports that would reveal identity or are not publicly available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-citation: use third person
rubrics_metrics.description: When referring to one’s own work, use the third person, rather than the first person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example guidance given: say 'Previously, Newell (Newell 1996) has shown that…' rather than 'In our previous work (Newell 1996) we have shown that….' Use third-person phrasing for self-citations to avoid revealing authorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-acceptance addition of identifying information
rubrics_metrics.description: Information that would identify the authors or their institutions may be added to the final camera-ready version for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a submission is accepted, add acknowledgments, author names, affiliations, and other identifying details when preparing the camera-ready version; omit them from the blinded submission.
